A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The complete main texts, equations, six figures, seventeen tables, and Appendices A–J are available and readable, supporting comparison despite rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments on ANES and MFQ, prompt mitigation results, sensitivity and human evaluations, misinformation detection, and a base-versus-RLHF comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and supplementary analyses in Appendices E–I.

M1.justification: The elicitation procedure, exemplar calculation, smoothing, and AWARENESS, FEEDBACK, and REASONING strategies remain the same. Renaming Believed Mean to Predicted Mean and rephrasing the awareness preamble do not substantively change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten ANES topics, thirty MFQ questions, and filtered Wang (2017) misinformation dataset. The political groups, domains, and evaluated scenarios are retained; the expanded MFQ description introduces no additional coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Gemini, Llama2-70b, Llama3-8b, and Qwen2.5-72b. Human comparators, the four-model misinformation comparison, and the Llama2 base-versus-chat comparison also retain their respective memberships.

E3.justification: Sample counts, filtering, scale reversals, model configurations, temperature settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Appendices E and G retain the same human-evaluation design, temperature sweep, and four misinformation prompt conditions.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same prompt consistency checks, temperature sensitivity experiment, human evaluation, exemplar comparison, misinformation controls, and RLHF analysis. Rewriting their explanations and moving displays adds no ablation or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both report twenty repetitions for the main analysis, ten runs per temperature setting, standard deviations, coefficients of variation, and response ranges. v3 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in Tables 1–15 are unchanged, including mitigation, misinformation, sensitivity, and RLHF results. Figures 2–6 retain their plotted outcomes, and no empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the exemplar and right-tail definitions, the ordering assumption, and Appendix A's smoothing formulation remain unchanged. Terminology and explanatory prose are revised without new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: analyzing political stereotypes through representative heuristics, finding exaggerated partisan predictions, and mitigating them through prompting. The rewritten framing introduces no distinct core contribution.

C2.justification: Sections 1–2 newly explain that some stereotypes lack empirical foundations and can arise from misinformation or propaganda. Section 6 explicitly describes κ as a proxy and emphasizes context-specific mitigation, while also making some descriptions more categorical. The existing population limitations and Appendix G's noncausal qualification remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v3 supplies a repository link and states that code is publicly released. Section 5.1 also explicitly documents aggregation at the MFQ dimension level. These are access and documentation changes, not evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jeoung, Diesner, and Kilicoglu (2023a), on first names and social commonsense reasoning, to support discussion of demographic conditioning. The existing StereoMap citation becomes 2023b; the remaining literature and overall cognitive-science positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, results, related work, discussion, and substantial appendix prose are extensively rewritten. Belief terminology becomes Prediction terminology, explanations are reorganized and expanded, and the title and conference-year header are edited. This is a substantial editorial revision despite stable scientific content.

P2.justification: All six figures and seventeen tables remain. Figure 1, Figure 4, and Table 8 receive terminology or label changes, numerous captions are rewritten, and displays are repositioned across the main text and appendices. The basic visual designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The code-access information, clearer terminology, and explicit qualification that stereotypes need not have empirical foundations provide limited improvements in usability and conceptual clarity. The scientific evidence is unchanged. These gains are tempered by more categorical mitigation wording: Table 3 still includes worsening cases, such as Llama3-8b ANES awareness κ of 16.89 versus baseline 10.84.
